critical_code_review_comments: routers/agent.py _execute_run: loop reads the entire run doc on every tick then acts; not atomic. Two overlapping _schedule() calls (e.g. approve twice on the same run) could double-drive a step. Consider a guard on status transitions running→running or a per-run asyncio.Lock.

routers/agent.py: STEP_TIMEOUT_SEC=45 is hard-coded. If a legit slow app takes ~50s the step will be marked failed and halt the whole run. Consider making it kind-specific (open_app slower than notify).

routers/agent.py _plan_with_llm: fenced-code stripping is fragile (text.strip('`') then substring by first { / last }). If LLM ever emits ```json{...}``` with braces inside code content the trim can misalign. A tolerant JSON extractor (regex or a couple of json.loads attempts) would be safer — same comment as iteration 28 for letters.

routers/agent.py cancel(): only updates commands whose status is queued/dispatched. If a companion picked up a command that is still 'running' remotely, cancel won't propagate — the step will just fail on timeout. Documenting or adding a cancel signal via the poll response could help.
routers/agent.py: no rate-limit or per-user quota on POST /api/agent/runs — each call is a Claude Sonnet 4.5 request. Consider a debounce or daily cap.
Agent.jsx: activeRun polling interval is 1500ms while running (reasonable) but never backs off; if network is flaky the UI may pile up requests. Consider AbortController per tick.
Agent.jsx: `showActive` includes 'completed' so a just-finished run stays pinned as 'current plan' — mildly confusing. Minor UX nit.
